plan.attnMode: attn_mode must be tp or dp
plan.epExceedsExperts: EP cannot exceed the expert count
plan.moeEpExceedsExperts: moe_ep cannot exceed the expert count
plan.moeEpExceedsEp: moe_ep({moeEp}) cannot exceed ep({ep}): expert ownership is a refinement of ep (protocol Q2)
plan.expertsNotDivisible: experts({experts}) must be divisible by moe_ep({moeEp})
plan.expertDomainOpen: expert domain is not closed: moe_ep({moeEp}) × moe_tp({moeTp}) must equal ep({ep}) × tp({tp}) (TRT-LLM Hybrid ETP)
plan.moeTpEqualsTp: without EP, moe_tp({moeTp}) must equal tp({tp}): DP shards experts via combined semantics (protocol Q4)
plan.epEqualsTpDp: when EP is enabled, ep must equal TP×DP={expected} (vLLM: EP_SIZE = TP_SIZE × DP_SIZE)

cost.disclaimer: Theoretical calculation; not simulation or prediction
cost.independent: P/D workloads, node counts, and parallel plans are saved independently; only the current phase is shown.
cost.theoretical: Cost is a theoretical estimate of graph-resident memory (weights, KV, KDA, declared buffers). Activation workspace, CUDA runtime, and comm scratch are runtime-unknown and not included. Roofline times are lower bounds. No scheduling, pipeline bubble, or transfer overlap simulation.
cost.chunkedSummary: Total uses {total} input tokens; peak uses {peak} tokens per chunk.
cost.kvBytesPerElementHelp: Fallback only: explicit node/cache dtype declarations (for example DSA index dtype) take precedence.
cost.macsOriginTitle: MACs totals by origin: formula-derived, summed from children, non-compute, or missing
cost.stageLine: Stage {stage} {weights} weights · {kv} KV · {state} KDA state · HBM ≈{hbm}
cost.unknownCompute: {count, plural, one {# operator has no cost formula.} other {# operators have no cost formula.}}
cost.weightsEstimate: Weights use a {bytes} B/parameter {quantization} estimate; checkpoint metadata can refine module exceptions.

valueSource.title: Weight-carrying nodes by value origin: checkpoint truth vs config-derived estimate

eta.detail: Vector/SFU rates are computed at 100% efficiency (rates.js falls back to eta.vector ?? 1 / eta.sfu ?? 1; resolveEfficiency does not emit these keys, so neither the sliders nor chip-level declarations reach them). ηF defaults to 0.7 as an adjustable assumption (principles §3.6) with no separate vector/SFU discount, so 1.0 is an explicit optimistic upper bound, not a measurement. The ηF slider does not affect vector/SFU paths.
